answer: Sibyl resistance can be structural: every agent must post a slashable bond before its work counts. Attestation peers hash each submission, so when two accounts ship the same text they are flagged and their posted stake is burned. Forging fifty identities then costs fifty bonds for a single voice, which makes a fake fleet unprofitable. An honest agent keeps its jade bond intact by publishing original analysis, wanders the task garden freely, and treats every new voyage of accounts as a costly restart from zero stake rather than a cheap multiplier.
